title: FlashSpec: lossless speculative decoding with a static-cache CUDA-graph fast path
description: FlashSpec is an open-source speculative-decoding engine for HuggingFace causal language models. Its sampling path (Leviathan et al. Algorithm 1) keeps the target model's output distribution, and its greedy path emits the target's argmax at every position. CI checks both on CPU: a chi-squared test on emitted tokens, and a token-for-token comparison with generate(do_sample=False). A batch-1 path on a static KV cache with CUDA graphs was measured on one model pair (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct verified by Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct), one Tesla T4, fp16, batch 1, with compile on: there it was faster than HuggingFace generate compiled the same way. Without compile it was slower than plain HuggingFace generate on most measured cells. The UCB1/Thompson draft selector is experimental: every measured run used one drafter. The Triton and assembly kernels are experimental and not on the generation critical path. The citable preprint is 10.5281/zenodo.20766119 (June 2026). paper/flashspec.tex is a later draft and is not itself a deposit.
notes: Metadata for a future Zenodo archive. The published record is 10.5281/zenodo.20766119, deposited 2026-06-19. Depositing a new version stays with the maintainer. Do not install flashspec==0.1.2; that package release was yanked. flashspec-asm-kernel 0.1.2 is a different package.
